messages:
Maria: Heads-up — over the past 45m the spot-gpu-us-west2 nodepool threw ~12 preemption events and cluster-autoscaler didn't bring fallback-nodes up fast enough. Several batch jobs got OOMKilled when they were re-scheduled. anyone else seeing this?
Sanjay: yep saw the same. CA logs show scale-up request accepted but node provisioning stuck in PROVISIONING for >3m.
InfraBot: [gcloud] Instance group 'spot-gpu-us-west2-pool' reported 9 preemptible terminations in the last 60 minutes.
Kai: Is this the new policy we rolled last week or just noisy spot market?
Maria: market spike — but also our CA config has aggressive scaleDownDelay. When the pool drops it tries to move pods but the fallback warm-pool uses on-demand GPUs with taints that many jobs don't tolerate.
Elaine: can we make critical batch jobs tolerate the fallback taint and prefer warm-pool? right now only prod-api is tolerant.
Sanjay: quick mitigation: reduce nodeGroups.unavailableThreshold in the CA and add a fallbackPriority for gpu-warm-pool. but that still means more $$.
Ops OnCall: Logging an incident (INC-2025-382). Notifying oncall rotation.
Maria: sample taint/toleration we can add to batch workloads: ```yaml
tolerations:
  - key: "gpu-fallback"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```
Kai: For node autoscaling, I think we should also add a kube-node-termination-handler that drains nodes on preemption notice and mark pods with PDB-aware eviction. Otherwise we lose big model checkpoints.
Sanjay: agreed. Also saw CA error: "scale up failed: insufficient instance quota in us-west2 for n1-gpu" — that explains provisioning hang. Maybe fallback should include cross-region option (us-west1) when local quota exhausted.
Maria: cross-region adds latency for GPUs using NFS mounts. For training jobs we can replicate checkpoints to object storage and prefer cross-region scheduling if job tolerates it.
Elaine: idea: add prioritized scheduling policy: 1) spot-gpu-us-west2, 2) spot-gpu-us-west1, 3) gpu-warm-on-demand. Have CA / scheduler-extender pick best pool based on time-to-provision and cost threshold.
Kai: we have a SchedulerExtender prototype. I can wire heuristics: provision_time_estimate = historical_median(provisioning_time) * (1 + spot_interrupt_rate). If estimate > 180s, route to fallback.
InfraBot: Note: GCP preemptible termination notice sample: "2025-01-14T15:03:21Z - instance instance-xyz will be terminated in 30s". Node-termination-handler handles this if deployed.
Maria: short term action items: @Kai add node-termination-handler to spot pools; @Sanjay tweak CA thresholds + cross-region fallback; @Elaine update batch job k8s templates with toleration and smaller PDBs for faster evict; @Ops OnCall monitor cost delta.
Sanjay: I'll also open a quota request with cloud to raise GPU quota in us-west2.
Ops OnCall: Marking incident as "monitoring". Will update if further preemptions.
Kai: quick config snippet for CA proposal: ```yaml
cluster-autoscaler:
  scaleDownDelayAfterAdd: 10m
  scaleDownDelayAfterDelete: 2m
  expandToZones: true
  priorities:
    - name: spot-us-west2
      weight: 0
    - name: spot-us-west1
      weight: 10
    - name: warm-on-demand
      weight: 100
```
Elaine: pinging ML infra owners about checkpoint replication so cross-region fallbacks are safer.
Maria: thanks — let's reconvene in 30m, posting followups here. :thumbsup:
InfraBot: Incident INC-2025-382 updated: status -> monitoring
Sanjay: update — quota request submitted (req-6789). ETA 48h.
Ops OnCall: last check: preemptions decreased but still above baseline. continuing to monitor.
